To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
life satisfaction (LS), in addition to positive affect (PA), and negative affect (NA), predicted student engagement and academic achievement.

life satisfaction is an independent predictor of student engagement and some academic achievement measures, and that the relationship between LS and achievement is moderated by gender, with boys showing higher LS-achievement correlations.

Life satisfaction (LS) is an important component of SWB that provides incremental validity over affect and other demographic variables in predicting engagement and achievement, and gender moderated these relationships.

the role that life satisfaction, a component of subjective well-being, plays in predicting student engagement in school and academic achievement.
the relationship between subjective well being (i.e. life satisfaction, PA, NA), engagement and academic achievement in a group of middle school students (N 1, 200).

the results of this study support the use of life satisfaction in addition to the use of positive and negative affect in the prediction of student engagement and academic achievement in middle school students.

the inclusion of life satisfaction as a component of SWB is warranted when predicting student functioning.
